item.title: Dubai teen built AI platform for breast cancer after losing grandmother at 10; took cancer awareness to India
item.description: Saiyette Aima’s journey began with her grandmother’s battle against breast cancer, driving her to make a significant impact. She spearheaded community-oriented fundraising and awareness campaigns, which flourished with local backing. Following this, Aima launched Pink for Purpose and started a YouTube channel to enhance her outreach. Her mission extended to India, providing free screening camps, which culminated in the innovative CareCheck, an AI tool for guiding breast health decisions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: As 9/11 attacks collapsed his office, a blind man's guide dog helped him down 78 flights to safety
item.description: During the harrowing 9/11 attacks, Michael Hingson's guide dog, Roselle, became his lifeline, leading him down seventy-eight floors from the north tower. Together with his colleague David Frank, they managed to escape the crumbling World Trade Center amid chaos. While firefighters bravely climbed upward, Hingson and Frank made their way to safety. In the aftermath, Hingson found solace through sharing their powerful story of trust and collaboration.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Mozart's melodies were less predictable, teen finds
item.description: Eighteen-year-old Linus Chen-Plotkin from Philadelphia has created a groundbreaking study on the genius of Mozart. Using statistical tests to evaluate melody predictability, he found that Mozart's music demonstrated significantly lower predictability than that of his contemporaries. This unique characteristic allowed him to both adhere to classical standards and surprise his audience, offering fresh insights into the nature of musical innovation and the essence of artistic excellence.

item.title: Toronto uses cold water from 83m beneath Lake Ontario to cool 200 buildings across downtown
item.description: In a bold move towards sustainability, Toronto harnesses the icy depths of Lake Ontario for its cooling systems. By drawing from eighty-three meters beneath the lake's surface, this network services two hundred buildings and spans over forty million square feet. This innovative strategy not only slashes electricity usage compared to traditional AC methods but also revamps a natural asset into core urban infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Mississippi teen who wrote an autism book for her sister finishes second at Miss America’s Teen
item.description: Mississippi teen Madalyn Sullivan has finished as first runner-up at Miss America’s Teen after representing her state at the national competition. An Oxford High School student, Sullivan founded Millie’s Mission, an initiative inspired by her sister’s autism diagnosis. She also co-authored the children’s book “Meet Millie” and donated copies to public libraries across all 82 Mississippi counties.

item.title: Phase Three Expansion: Broad Metro buys final 65 acres for $4.6 million; city backs $200m plan
item.description: Broad Metro LLC has successfully acquired sixty-five acres to launch the third phase of Stadium Trace Village. This ambitious expansion will feature a blend of retail spaces, medical facilities, and professional offices, alongside luxury residential options in the upper sections. The Hoover City Council has endorsed this initiative by approving an economic development agreement, marking a pivotal advancement in the long-term growth strategy of the project.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Lightning Damages Mansion Turret: Fire chars historic Maple Street landmark; store below stays open
item.description: A dramatic lightning strike set the turret of a historic mansion in Georgia ablaze on Saturday night. Firefighters successfully contained the fire to the upper exterior, limiting its impact. The steeple and balcony suffered considerable damage, but thankfully, the business within the mansion emerged largely unscathed. Exterior repairs are scheduled as operations at the store proceed with minimal disruption.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Six people buried in a rare Viking Age grave reveal violence, family ties, and Baltic ancestry
item.description: A rare ninth-century burial in Latvia revealed violence and family connections. Ancient DNA showed father and son relationships among the six individuals. Three men bore sharp-force injuries, suggesting a violent incident occurred. Genetic analysis placed the group closer to local Baltic populations. This unusual grave offers insights into Viking Age Semigallian life and kinship.

item.title: Dam Removal Reopens Habitat: Virginia project reconnects 127 miles; migratory fish return upstream
item.description: In 2014, the removal of Harvell Dam revitalized over 120 miles of river, providing essential upstream habitats for migratory fish. Observations from state biologists and anglers confirmed fish migrating upstream post-demolition. This collaborative restoration project united various agencies and organizations, successfully restoring the river's free-flowing state and enhancing benefits for both aquatic life and recreational activities.

item.title: Texas’ Bahia Grande stayed dry for 70 years before tides brought wildlife back
item.description: Bahia Grande, a Texas wetland, was dry for over seventy years. Human activity disrupted tidal pathways, causing ecological loss and dust problems. Conservation efforts restored tidal connections in two thousand six, bringing back water. Wildlife, including thousands of birds, quickly returned to the revitalized habitat. This restoration highlights the importance of water flow for wetland function.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Suborno Bari: The young maths prodigy who caught Barack Obama’s attention
item.description: Suborno Isaac Bari, a 12-year-old student, graduated high school after skipping several grades. He began attending university-level classes and lecturing in India at age seven. Bari entered New York University with plans to complete his degree by age 14. His parents, both educators, inspired his ambition to teach mathematics and physics. He also pursued interests in debate, painting, and playing the piano.

item.title: In 1895, lightning ignited a West Virginia gas well; flames soared 200 feet as crowds watched
item.description: In a remarkable display, a West Virginia gas well suffered a fiery explosion triggered by a lightning strike. Discovered in 1895, this vast gas reservoir was tough to control with the limited technology of the era. For two hours, flames leaped 150 to 200 feet into the sky until the force of the escaping gas extinguished itself.
